# `type-narrowed`

Type narrowed

| | |
|---|---|
| **Kind** | `wire` |
| **Default severity** | `error` in requests, `info` in responses |
| **Rule IDs** | `type-narrowed` (both directions), `type-narrowed-in-request`, `type-narrowed-in-response` |
| **Status** | Planned (M5) |
| **Group** | Schemas ([RULES.md section 7](../../RULES.md)) |

## What it detects

The type now accepts less, e.g. `number` → `integer`.

## Why this default

In requests: clients sending the removed kinds of values are rejected. In responses: clients receive a subset of what they handled.

## Example

_No example yet: one is added with the rule's test case when the rule is implemented._

## Policy options

Every rule takes `severity` (`error`, `warn`, `info` or `off`), `fix` and `explanation` in the policy file, for the generic ID or any variant ID above (the more specific ID wins). The policy file arrives in M6; see [POLICY.md](../../POLICY.md).

```yaml
rules:
  type-narrowed: info
```

## How to fix

In requests, keep accepting the old type.
